title: Ceramic coating vs wax for Calgary winters
description: How wax, sealants and ceramic coatings differ, how long each lasts against Calgary road salt and mag chloride, and which makes sense for how long you keep the vehicle.
excerpt: Wax sits on the paint for weeks. A ceramic coating bonds to it for years. How they compare against salt brine, mag chloride and car-wash brushes.

sections.heading: What wax does well
paragraphs: Carnauba wax adds warmth and gloss and is easy to apply. It's also soft and sits on top of the paint, so detergents, road salt and heat wear it off in weeks. Through a Calgary winter, it's often gone after a few washes.

sections.heading: Sealants: the middle ground
paragraphs: Synthetic sealants bond better than wax and last months rather than weeks. They're a good fit for a vehicle that gets detailed a few times a year and doesn't need long-term protection.

sections.heading: Ceramic coatings: years, not months
paragraphs: A ceramic coating chemically bonds to the clear coat and forms a hard, slick layer. Salt brine and mag chloride rinse off instead of sitting on the paint, washing gets faster, and the gloss holds for years depending on the product tier.
It isn't armour. A coating won't stop rock chips; that's what paint protection film is for. And the paint should be corrected first, because a coating locks in whatever is underneath it.

sections.heading: Which one to pick
paragraphs: Keeping the vehicle a year or two: a sealant on a regular schedule. Keeping it five years or longer, or it's new: a coating usually costs less per year than repeated sealants, and makes every winter wash easier.
